newsitem.title: USA: Owens Corning sees 97 EPS $4.80-$5.00 range.
newsitem.headline: Owens Corning sees 97 EPS $4.80-$5.00 range.

text.p: Owens Corning said on Thursday it was comfortable with estimates for earnings in the range of $4.80-$5.00 per diluted share for 1997, fueled by growth in income from operations.
The company said income from operations would grow in the range of 10 to 15 percent in 1997, but would somewhat offset by a higher tax rate.
According to First Call, analysts's consensus estimate for 1997 was $5.06 per share.

"We are confident that we'll reach $5 billion in sales by 1999," Glen Hiner, Owens Corning chairman, said in a statement. "With the initiatives already in place and our continuing focus on growth and productivity, we are looking forward to another record year in 1997."

The company reported fourth quarter fully diluted earnings of $1.25 per share versus $1.21 per share in the year-ago quarter. Fourth quarter 1996 net income included a pretax charge of $43 million for restructuring and other actions, as well as one-time tax benefits.
The fourth quarter 1995 included a $0.15 per share benefit from tax-loss benefit, the company said.

Hiner said the company expected sales momentum established in building materials in North America during 1996 to continue and expected a turnaround in Europe in the second half of 1997. Building materials sales increased by 12 percent for the quarter and the year, the company said.

About half of that growth came from acquisitions completed by the company in 1995 and 1996, it said. Earnings from ongoing operations increased 22 percent for the quarter and 14 percent for the year in building materials, it said.
